title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity
talk_summary: Kevin Hou describes Google Antigravity's shift to 'agent teams' built on three primitives: dynamically generated sub-agents, long-lived 'sidecar' trigger processes, and generative UI. The core argument is to build primitives that scale with model intelligence rather than hard-coding deterministic scaffolding, and he cites a 93-sub-agent, 12-hour, $1k OS-kernel build as evidence.

takeaways.technique: Lead agent dynamically spawns specialized sub-agents
takeaways.what_they_do: A single lead agent decomposes the task and generates sub-agents on the fly, each with its own role, prompt, and even a different model, running in parallel across sandboxes.
A long-lived sidecar process listens to external events (webhooks, cron, GitHub PRs, SMS) and lets the agent set its own triggers, rather than polling inside a run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It allows the model to listen to the outside world and set up its own triggers for things that might happen. For example, this could be SMS messages. This could be web hooks, cron jobs, hooking it up to GitHub PRs

takeaways.what_they_do: For eval deltas, a research agent proposes ~100 hypotheses, then one sub-agent per hypothesis drills in parallel and maps back to a single report.
takeaways.numbers: automated 90% of the side-by-side eval workflow

takeaways.what_they_do: Researchers ask the agent in natural language about an eval; the agent crunches numbers, computes deltas, and generates an interactive report instead of hand-writing notebooks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: researchers were able to automate 90% of this workflow by simply asking the agent about the eval in question using natural language
takeaways.numbers: 90% of workflow automated; minutes vs manual

takeaways.technique: Skills files as the only user input
takeaways.what_they_do: Users load a skills file describing the workflow and then just ask; the agent is primed with repo/monorepo knowledge and skills to execute the whole pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All the user had to do was load up a skills file and ask away.

takeaways.what_they_do: Sub-agents can run in different execution environments (local sandbox or remote execution system) chosen per sub-agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They can operate in different types of secure environments be it a sandbox be it a remote execution system
